strengths_deep_dive: Sadagaat maintains high financial health and direct impact orientation. In FY2024, the organization spent <cite id="1">97.7% of its budget directly on programs</cite>, outperforming the 89.2% median for peer humanitarian organizations. Independent evaluator Charity Navigator awarded Sadagaat <cite id="1">an overall score of 97.5/100</cite>, backed by full points in leadership and culture. Furthermore, the organization holds a Candid Platinum Seal of Transparency, demonstrating clear operational reporting.
rich_narrative.summary: Sadagaat provides essential aid through water, health, and education programs while maintaining high financial efficiency. Founded in 2002, the organization focuses on serving vulnerable populations in Sudan and the United States, particularly targeting educational support for non-enrolled and blind children <cite id="5">through dedicated program sectors</cite>. In FY2024, Sadagaat managed <cite id="3">$2,368,977 in total revenue</cite>, reflecting significant institutional expansion over recent years. The organization operates as a verified <cite id="2">zakat-eligible charity</cite>, directing gifts toward fundamental needs across water, healthcare, feeding, and educational initiatives <cite id="2">in accordance with Islamic principles</cite>. Sadagaat demonstrates strong operational efficiency, directing <cite id="1">97.7% of expenses to program activities</cite> in FY2024. This performance exceeds the humanitarian peer median of 89.2% and comfortably surpasses the 75% industry standard. The charity has earned <cite id="1">a 97.5/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite> along with a Candid Platinum Seal of Transparency. However, its intensive direct service model generates a high cost per beneficiary of $2,064.84, and the organization currently lacks a formally documented theory of change to outline long-term outcomes.
